title: Niche topics (1): returns, costs, tax and exits
objectives: Explain why a client's return can differ from the strategy return.
List hidden costs beyond the headline fee.
body_md:
These rarely come up at onboarding but drive most PMS complaints and surprises.

| Topic | What to explain | Investor takeaway |
|---|---|---|
| Strategy return vs your return | Each client's portfolio is built at a different time and price, so their return can differ from the published strategy return. | Ask for your own account's after-fee return. |
| Hidden costs | Brokerage, custody and demat charges, GST on fees and profit share add up beyond the headline fee. | Ask for the all-in cost, not just the management fee. |
| Tax on trading | Every sale by the manager is a capital gains event for the client; high turnover can mean a bigger tax bill. Tax treatment of PMS fees is not straightforward. | Discuss turnover and tax with your CA. |
| Exit loads | Exit loads are capped by SEBI (up to 3% in year 1, 2% in year 2, 1% in year 3) and set in each agreement. | Check your agreement before investing. |
| Direct onboarding | Clients can invest directly without a distributor; explain selection, monitoring and service as our value. | You have a direct option; know what a distributor adds. |
example: A client's account is 4% below the published strategy return. You explain entry timing and cash flows, and show the account's own after-fee return against the benchmark.
say: Ask for the all-in cost, not just the management fee.
Check your agreement for the exit load before investing.
never: The strategy return is your return.

check.q: What are the SEBI caps on PMS exit loads?
o: Up to 3% in year 1, 2% in year 2 and 1% in year 3
1% flat for the first year only
No exit load is allowed in PMS
check.why: The actual load is set in each agreement, within these caps.

check.q: Which is a "hidden cost" beyond the headline PMS fee?
o: GST on fees and profit share, brokerage, custody and demat charges
check.why: Ask for the all-in cost, not just the management fee.

check.q: Which is a cost that sits beyond the headline PMS management fee?
check.why: Brokerage, custody and demat charges, and GST add up beyond the headline fee.
